title: Software Engineer, Cornell AI 4 Cities Lab
summary: Software engineer on the Urban AI Automation Team, building tools that let AI agents analyze NYC Open Data geospatial datasets.
body:
- Developing MCP server letting AI agents analyze NYC Open Data geospatial datasets, targeting 10+ indicators under 20 min.
- Building DAG-based workflow engine that validates and runs agent-authored tool-call pipelines with parallel execution.
- Implementing replay from content-hashed data extracts so researchers can reproduce past results and detect data drift.

title: Software Engineer Intern, Goldman Sachs
summary: Data Engineering internship building an agentic data-discovery pipeline that automates vendor data curation and publication to the firm's data marketplace, cutting turnaround time from 3+ days to 20 minutes.
body:
- Developed agentic data-discovery pipeline that automates vendor data curation and publication to the firm's data marketplace, cutting turnaround time from 3+ days to 20 minutes.
- Built agentic skill for dataset metadata generation, and Python tag-matching algorithm, 98% faster execution than manual process.
- Wrote Python scripts to make classification and tag-matching deterministic, added human-in-the-loop review before publishing via API, and wrote 18 evals that passed before rollout.
- Onboarded vendor data into firm's lakehouse via AWS S3 pipeline; extended it to support .gz for expanded ingestion coverage.

title: Software Engineer Intern, Walmart Global Tech
summary: Implemented search filtering for a compliance portal, cutting search time from 5+ minutes to under 5 seconds across 600+ compliance rules.
body:
- Implemented search filtering for compliance portal, cutting search time from 5+ mins to <5s across 600+ compliance rules.
- Developed Java algorithm that dynamically filters 600+ rules across 8+ parameters while synchronizing results with search queries, and built Spring Boot API endpoint with PostgreSQL to fetch rules by service tag.
- Created reusable React/TypeScript UI filtering components powering rule search for 20+ business users.
- Implemented unit, integration, and E2E tests (JUnit, Spring Test, Jest); deployed with Kubernetes and Docker.

title: Director of Projects, ACM UTD
summary: Ran the 10-week project program for ACM UTD, the largest CS organization at UTD (800+ members), coaching 11 project team leads and guiding 50+ students.
body: - Ran ACM's 10-week project program: coached 11 project team leads and guided 50+ students through workshops and project development sessions; worked with mentors from CBRE, JPMC, Amazon.

title: Project Manager, ACM UTD
summary: Led 2 teams of 4 developers through the full software development lifecycle at ACM UTD, running sprint planning and weekly standups to ship full-stack applications.
body:
- Directly led 2 teams of 4 developers through the full software development lifecycle, running sprint planning and weekly standups to ship full-stack applications (React, Node, MongoDB, AWS).
- Promoted to Director of Projects.

title: Cascading Flight-Delay Risk Model
summary: Cascading-delay risk model for DFW airport, presented to American Airlines as 1 of 6 finalists among 30 teams in the American Airlines Data Challenge.
body:
- Built a cascading-delay risk identification model specialized to DFW airport, presented to AA as 1 of 6 finalists among 30 teams.
- Performed data fusion across multi-source aviation data (flight, weather, and atmospheric datasets), reconciling mismatched time granularities and join keys into a unified training set.
- Engineered 40+ features to train 4-layer PyTorch neural network flagging flights at high risk of propagating delays with 0.65 F1.

title: Insyte
summary: Full-stack multi-agent property search platform built for the CBRE HackUTD Challenge, turning natural language queries into mapped properties and insights.
body:
- Architected full-stack multi-agent property search platform for CBRE HackUTD Challenge so property managers can turn natural language queries into mapped properties and insights across 90+ properties in under 10s.
- Leveraged LLM agents for query parsing and filter selection, and Python property matching with 92% accuracy over 50 queries.

title: UTD Capstone: Disaster Damage Assessment
summary: Led development of a vision-language model pipeline on a team of 6 to classify property-level damage severity from satellite images, with a map dashboard and a chatbot grounded in the damage data.
body:
- Led development of VLM pipeline (LLaVA 1.5-7B, Python) to classify property-level damage severity across 4000+ buildings from 68 satellite images on a team of 6, achieving 60.3% accuracy against FEMA ground-truth labels.
- Built React.js/Mapbox dashboard rendering building-level damage heatmaps over pre/post disaster imagery from AWS S3.
- Built OpenAI chatbot grounded in VLM damage data, responding to queries in chat and with live map actions/navigation.
